title: [Bug]: PD-admitted Mamba request is spec-padded before prefill completes, then align split truncates the 8-token window to 5
body:
## Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment and topology</summary>

```text
vLLM: v0.27.1, tag commit 6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac
Relevant merged change: #51113
  release commit: 3f9fc83067cdd377c51d58ad949380a164bee260
  upstream commit: c56f169d9ae46ca420617e2cf5f0c9135da0f651

Backend: vLLM Ascend, source installation from main plus Kimi-K3 support
Python: 3.11.10
Device: Ascend NPU
Engine: V1 with async scheduling

Deployment:
  - disaggregated prefill/decode using MooncakeConnectorV1
  - 2 prefill instances and 2 decode instances
  - each instance: TP=16
  - each P/D group: DP=2, one local DP rank per node
  - enable_prefix_caching=true
  - mamba_cache_mode=align on both P and D
  - Mamba/scheduler block size=384
  - max_model_len=133120
  - max_num_batched_tokens=8192
  - max_num_seqs=16
  - speculative method=DSpark, K=7, parallel draft TP=16

Model: Kimi-K3 hybrid attention/Mamba target with a compatible DSpark draft model.
For this scheduling/metadata investigation only, the target was loaded in a
10/93-layer reduced debug mode. This makes generated text unsuitable for model
quality evaluation, but does not change the scheduler transition described
below: prompt length, external-computed-token count, Mamba block split,
scheduled token count, or speculative placeholder count.

The same scheduler ordering is still present on vLLM main at
1ebff996a118cdc6e831c521c839d29ffe47d30f (checked 2026-08-30).
```

The full `collect_env.py` output is not attached because the reproduction ran
on an isolated multi-node environment. The values above are taken from the
startup and engine logs. Private host addresses, model paths, engine IDs and
request IDs have been removed.

</details>

## Describe the bug

### Summary

On a PD decode worker, a newly admitted request may have all but the last prompt
token supplied by the KV connector. If running decode requests are already in
the batch, the waiting-request scheduling path treats the one remaining token
as a new decode and pads it from 1 token to `1 + K` tokens.

For a hybrid Mamba model in `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, #51113 correctly clips
a prefill-like span that starts mid-block so it cannot cross the next Mamba
boundary. In our case the padded 8-token span starts at 379 and is clipped at
384, leaving only 5 physical query tokens. However, `pad_spec_decode` remains
true and the scheduler still publishes 7 speculative placeholders.

This creates a request-local contract violation:

```text
logical speculative window: 1 target + 7 drafts = 8
physical target span after Mamba split:          5
speculative placeholders/rejection window:      7
```

The global flattened batch shapes remain valid. The failure occurs when the
proposer interprets the 5-token request row using a 7-token rejection window.
On the Ascend DSpark backend this produces an invalid request-local position and
slot mapping and terminates the engine.

This is not a request to revert #51113. Its Mamba boundary protection is
required to prevent recurrent-state cache poisoning. The missing invariant is
that a synthetically padded speculative window must either survive all later
scheduler limiters atomically, or the padding must be cancelled for that
request.

### Deployment/startup configuration

The actual deployment uses a small wrapper to start one local DP rank on each
node. The following is a sanitized equivalent of the startup strategy:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROLE="$1"       # producer or consumer
DP_RANK="$2"    # 0 or 1 within the P group / D group
DP_ADDR="$3"    # shared coordinator address for that group
KV_PORT="$4"

export VLLM_USE_V1=1
export VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_MLAPO=1

SPEC_CONFIG='{
  "method": "dspark",
  "model": "<compatible-dspark-model>",
  "num_speculative_tokens": 7,
  "draft_tensor_parallel_size": 16,
  "max_model_len": 4096,
  "draft_sample_method": "greedy",
  "enforce_eager": true
}'

KV_CONFIG="{
  \"kv_connector\": \"MooncakeConnectorV1\",
  \"kv_role\": \"kv_${ROLE}\",
  \"kv_buffer_device\": \"npu\",
  \"kv_port\": ${KV_PORT},
  \"kv_connector_extra_config\": {
    \"prefill\": {\"dp_size\": 2, \"tp_size\": 16},
    \"decode\": {\"dp_size\": 2, \"tp_size\": 16}
  }
}"

vllm serve <kimi-k3-target-model> \
  --served-model-name kimi-k3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --data-parallel-rank "${DP_RANK}" \
  --data-parallel-address "${DP_ADDR}" \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --max-model-len 133120 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --speculative-config "${SPEC_CONFIG}" \
  --kv-transfer-config "${KV_CONFIG}"
```

The Ascend platform selects `mamba_cache_mode=align` when prefix caching is
enabled and resolves the common scheduler/Mamba block size to 384. P and D use
the same cache mode and logical KV-manager group topology.

### Trigger conditions

All of the following are needed for the observed frame:

1. A hybrid Mamba/GDN model with `mamba_cache_mode=align`.
2. Speculative decoding with a fixed `K` (`K=7` here).
3. A PD consumer request admitted with an unaligned external prefix. In the
   failing request, `num_prompt_tokens=380` and the D scheduler starts from
   `num_computed_tokens=379`.
4. At least one normal decode request is already scheduled in the same step,
   while no other prefill has yet been scheduled. This satisfies the
   waiting-request `pad_spec_decode` condition.
5. Padding creates an interval that crosses the next Mamba boundary:
   `[379, 379 + 1 + 7) = [379, 387)` crosses 384.
6. `_mamba_block_aligned_split()` clips the physical interval to `[379,384)`,
   but the scheduler retains 7 speculative placeholders.
7. The proposer subsequently applies the full 7-token rejection/proposal
   semantics to this 5-token request row.

A single 380-token request normally does **not** reproduce the failure. It first
schedules the one remaining prompt token alone and enters ordinary decode in
the next step. The mixed running-decode/new-PD-request batch is important.

### Workload used to trigger the mixed batch

The original fatal frame was observed during a concurrent GPQA workload. We
then reduced the traffic pattern to the following controlled case:

1. Use `/tokenize` to construct a prompt with exactly 380 tokens.
2. Start four long-running decode requests (`temperature=0`,
   `max_tokens=768`) so both D schedulers have running decode rows.
3. Wait two seconds.
4. Concurrently submit twelve identical 380-token completion requests through
   the 2P+2D proxy.

Sanitized client outline:

```bash
# Keep decode batches active.
for i in $(seq 1 4); do
  curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{
      "model":"kimi-k3",
      "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<long deterministic request>"}],
      "temperature":0,
      "max_tokens":768,
      "stream":false
    }' \
    http://<pd-proxy>/v1/chat/completions >"runner_${i}.json" &
done

sleep 2

# The prompt in exact_380.json was verified by /tokenize to contain 380 tokens.
for i in $(seq 1 12); do
  curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data-binary @exact_380.json \
    http://<pd-proxy>/v1/completions >"exact_380_${i}.json" &
done
wait
```

`exact_380.json`:

```json
{
  "model": "kimi-k3",
  "prompt": "<neutral repeated text tokenized to exactly 380 tokens>",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 16,
  "stream": false
}
```

The controlled workload deterministically reaches the same scheduler state on
both D instances (`start=379, requested=8, result=5, end=384`). The fatal
unpatched metadata frame quoted below comes from the original concurrent GPQA
run; the controlled workload was also used for subsequent isolation and fix
validation.

### Exact scheduler transition

The relevant waiting-request path currently behaves as follows:

```text
request.num_prompt_tokens = 380
num_computed_tokens        = 379  # external PD prefix ends here
real remaining prompt      = 1
num_spec_tokens            = 7

padding before split:
  num_new_tokens = 1 + 7 = 8
  pad_spec_decode = true

Mamba align split (#51113):
  start               = 379
  next_block_boundary = 384
  requested           = 8
  returned            = 384 - 379 = 5

scheduler output:
  num_scheduled_tokens[request]          = 5
  scheduled_spec_decode_tokens[request] = [-1] * 7
```

The ordering is visible in `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: the waiting path
sets `pad_spec_decode`, `_mamba_block_aligned_split()` is called later, and the
placeholder list is populated after slot allocation without checking whether
the padded width survived.

### Observed result

The failing batch contained 12 requests:

```text
num_scheduled_tokens = [5, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8]
total_num_scheduled_tokens = 93 = 5 + 11 * 8
query_start_loc.shape = [13]
input_ids.shape = [93]
```

Therefore the batch-level shapes are internally consistent. Only request row 0
is semantically invalid:

```text
prompt_tokens     = 380
computed_tokens   = 379
scheduled_tokens  = 5
num_ctx           = 5
seq_len           = 384
num_rejected      = 7
valid_ctx_end     = 5 - 7 = -2

expected query positions = [377, 378, 379, 380, 381, 382, 383]
actual query positions   = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
actual query slots       = [-1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1]
metadata_valid           = false
```

The first fatal error is:

```text
RuntimeError: Invalid DSpark input metadata; see DSPARK_METADATA_MISMATCH
for request index 0, kv-cache group 0.

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 1010, in worker_busy_loop
    output = func(*args, **kwargs)
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py", line 714, in sample_tokens
    return self.model_runner.sample_tokens(grammar_output)
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 2380, in sample_tokens
    propose_draft_token_ids(sampler_output.sampled_token_ids)
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 1708, in propose_draft_token_ids
    draft_token_ids = self.drafter._propose(...)
  File "vllm_ascend/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py", line 827, in _propose
    ... = self.set_inputs_first_pass(...)
  File "vllm_ascend/spec_decode/dspark_proposer.py", line 541, in set_inputs_first_pass
    raise RuntimeError(...)
```

Without the diagnostic guard, the invalid position/slot mapping would proceed
toward the device kernel. The guard turns it into a deterministic host-side
failure instead of a possible device-side out-of-bounds access.

### Isolation and validation results

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Small end-to-end PD request | HTTP 200; Mooncake transfer succeeds |
| One exact 380-token request without active decode traffic | Schedules 1 prompt token, then normal 8-token decode; no 5-vs-7 frame |
| Concurrent GPQA, mixed new PD admissions and running decode rows | Reproduces fatal `scheduled=5`, `num_rejected=7`, `valid_ctx_end=-2` frame |
| Controlled 4 long runners + 12 exact-380 requests | Reaches `start=379, requested=8, result=5, end=384` on both D instances |
| Temporarily restore the pre-#51113 `next_boundary <= last_cache_position` predicate | No 384 split and no metadata error, but reintroduces the prefix-cache poisoning fixed by #51113; not an acceptable fix |
| Keep #51113 and cancel/degrade speculative processing for the short request row | All requests return HTTP 200; no invalid metadata; subsequent scheduling continues from 384 |
| Keep #51113 and rebuild the DSpark anchor from the valid accepted end | All requests return HTTP 200; no invalid metadata; normal rows in the same mixed batch remain speculative |

The last two experiments confirm that the 384 stop itself is valid and that the
failure is the stale logical speculative width after the physical span is
shortened. They are backend-side experiments, not proposed as the preferred
upstream fix.

### Expected behavior

The last uncached prompt token on a PD consumer should remain a prefill token.
It should be scheduled alone, and speculative decode should begin on a later
step after the request has crossed the prefill/decode phase boundary.

More generally, when a scheduler marks a request as synthetically padded for
speculative decode, the final physical width after all limiters must be exactly
the padded width. If a Mamba split, token budget, encoder cap, long-prefill cap,
or any later limiter shortens it, the scheduler must cancel the synthetic
padding and not emit `K` placeholders for the shortened row.

### Suspected scheduler fix

The minimal phase guard is the same distinction discussed in #49495: do not
classify `num_new_tokens == 1` as a new decode solely by token count. Require
that prompt prefill has actually completed:

```diff
 if (
     (self.num_spec_tokens > 0 and self.dynamic_sd_lookup is None)
     and self.num_sampled_tokens_per_step > 0
     and num_new_tokens == 1
+    and num_computed_tokens >= request.num_prompt_tokens
     and (scheduled_running_reqs and not prefill_scheduled)
 ):
```

For the failing PD request, `379 < 380`, so it would schedule the one real prompt
token and would not advertise seven draft placeholders.

A defensive invariant should also be considered after all token-count limiters:

```text
if pad_spec_decode and final_num_new_tokens != padded_num_tokens:
    cancel speculative padding for this request
    schedule only its real remaining token(s)
    do not populate scheduled_spec_decode_tokens for this row
```

This would protect against future limiters that can shorten a padded window,
not only Mamba alignment.

Suggested regression test:

```text
hybrid Mamba align scheduler, block_size=384, K=7
one running decode request
one waiting request with prompt_tokens=380
connector reports external_computed_tokens=379

expected:
  num_scheduled_tokens[new_request] == 1
  new_request not in scheduled_spec_decode_tokens

must not produce:
  num_scheduled_tokens[new_request] == 5
  len(scheduled_spec_decode_tokens[new_request]) == 7
```

It would also be useful to parameterize this test for generic MTP/EAGLE. The
scheduler condition and window atomicity are not DSpark-specific, although the
exact error manifestation is backend/proposer-dependent.

### Related issues and PRs

- #51113 — required Mamba align boundary correctness; this report describes an
  interaction exposed by that fix, not a reason to revert it.
- #49495 — another case where a one-token prefill remainder is mistaken for a
  new decode by the padded waiting-request optimization.
- #53505 — related hybrid Mamba + KV connector + speculative-decoding family,
  but it reports recurrent-state corruption through connector prefix-cache
  reconciliation rather than this 5-token/7-placeholder mismatch.

### Before submitting a new issue

- [x] Searched existing open and closed issues, including #49495 and #53505.
- [x] Removed private hosts, credentials, paths, engine IDs and request IDs from
  the report.
